answer.text:
At the All-Ohio meet at Ohio State, the Ohio Wesleyan women's track team set three new school records in relays [Source 1]. The 880-yard relay team composed of sophomore Pebbles Muller, freshmen Amanda Osborn and Lynn Rhoden, and senior Sabrina Spencer placed sixth, bettering the 1979 record of 1:51.2 by one second [Source 1]. Additionally, the distance medley relay team of freshmen Liz Einfeldt, Nena Lenfest, Barb Sweeney, and junior Margie Morris placed fifth with a time of 13:17.1, breaking the previous year's record of 13:18 [Source 1]. Finally, Einfeldt, Lenfest, Sweeney, and sophomore Lisa Foster ran a 10:14 in the two-mile relay, surpassing last year's record of 10:20 [Source 1].

answer.text:
## Communications Infrastructure in 1987

In 1987, Ohio Wesleyan University recognized that its telephone system, which had been installed in 1974, was severely outdated and inadequate [1987-03-25-25]. The system caused widespread frustration among students, parents, and faculty due to frequent busy signals, lost calls, and long waits for a dial tone or operator assistance [1987-10-14-3, 1987-03-25-25]. To address these issues, the Board of Trustees approved a $50,000 feasibility study in late September 1987 to research renovating the telecommunications setup [1987-10-14-3]. Louis Szalontai, vice president of business affairs, explained that the funding was used to hire a professional consultant to evaluate new technologies, leasing options, and purchasing costs as part of an overhaul aimed at completing a new system by 1992 [1987-10-14-3].

## Academic Support in 2000

To address fragmented academic assistance across campus, OWU opened the **Academic Resource Center (ARC)** in the fall of 2000 on the third floor of the R. W. Corns Building [2000-09-13-3]. Directed by Donna Dawson, the ARC successfully combined three previously scattered support services into one centralized location: the Academic Skills Office, the Writing Resource Center (both formerly housed in University Hall), and the Qualitative Skills Center (formerly located in Ham-Wil) [2000-09-13-3]. By housing these programs together alongside study space, computers, and reference materials, the university streamlined resources to provide students with comprehensive assistance for writing, organizational skills, test preparation, stress management, and quantitative subjects [2000-09-13-3].

answer.text: Austin Hall closed in 1984, and plans to convert the residence hall into Austin Manor—a living unit for students and retired alumni—were established in the fall of 1986 [Source 1]. Although financing was arranged the following year, the project required tax credit approval due to its status as a historic site [Source 1]. Following an appeal, the credit was successfully approved, allowing renovation work to begin [Source 1]. University President David Warren estimated that the building would be ready for an occupant by November or December [Source 1].

answer.text:
## Early Childhood Center Support in 1997

Established for preschool-aged children between three and five years old, the Early Childhood Center (ECC) provided hands-on, sensory-based learning support [1997-01-22-17]. The learning environment emphasized self-exploration and imagination through activities such as observing and feeding animals in aquariums, constructing miniature houses, cutting snacks, and engaging in nature projects that stemmed from the children's own interests [1997-01-22-17]. The ECC was staffed by professional teachers as well as 29 Ohio Wesleyan University students who worked through work-study and Student Assistantship programs to interact with, assist, and encourage the children [1997-01-22-17]. ![an OWU student assists a child with a project at the Early Childhood Center](https://pub-6b4b0bceb63e48c1af6578ad09beb2e5.r2.dev/1997-01-22/images/0005_Page%205_img1.webp)

## Academic Resource Center Support in 2000

In contrast, the Academic Resource Center (ARC), established in the R. W. Corns Building in 2000, provided academic support services tailored for Ohio Wesleyan college students [2000-09-13-3]. The ARC brought together three previously separate entities: the Academic Skills Office, the Writing Resource Center, and the Qualitative Skills Center [2000-09-13-3]. Rather than sensory play, the ARC offered practical academic resources including study space, computers, writing reference materials, and targeted tutoring [2000-09-13-3]. Staffed by director Donna Dawson, English department faculty, psychology-trained interns, and peer tutors, the center offered assistance with writing papers, resumes, standardized test preparation, organizational skills, stress management, and quantitative subjects like math and economics up to Calculus II [2000-09-13-3].
